# How the metro areas are drawn

[All metro areas](data-sources.md)

The app covers six metro areas. This page says which counties each one has and why: first the rules, then how each area follows them.

## Rules

1. **Whole counties.** Each metro area is a list of whole counties. In Connecticut, which replaced its counties with planning regions in 2022, it is a list of planning regions.
2. **The government's metro areas first.** An area starts from the US government's own metro area around its city, as defined by the Office of Management and Budget in OMB Bulletin 23-01: the combined statistical area, which joins neighboring metro areas that many people commute between, or the metropolitan statistical area where there is no combined one.
3. **Names from Wikipedia.** An area is called by the name of its English Wikipedia article, such as Greater Boston or Lehigh Valley, rather than by the government's long list of cities.
4. **Islands.** A county that can only be reached by boat, where the boats leave from a metro area, is part of that area, even where the government leaves it out.
5. **Changes.** Where the government's area doesn't match where people travel, a county can move to the next area, and an area can be split in two or joined with its neighbor. Each area below says what changed and why.
6. **Where the app works.** Only in an area's counties, and there near its trains, buses and ferries: the far parts of large rural counties, at the service area's outer edge, are outside it, and the map in the README shows only the parts inside. A part of an area's counties that lies between two parts of the service area is in too, even with no stop nearby, so the service area has no holes: Salisbury, Connecticut, and Sheffield, Massachusetts, are in for that reason. A pier or a boat on the water, which is in no county, counts in the nearest one. Where you are, or a place you pick, still counts up to 15 km beyond the service area, in the nearest of the areas' counties, so the app doesn't say you are outside just over its edge.
7. **Edges.** Where an area's own buses or trains run into the next county, that county is added to the area, and only the part near their stops is in the service area.
8. **One piece.** Each area is one piece, drawn on the app's map as a single dashed ring. Where an area has islands off its coast, the water between them and the mainland is in the service area too, and over the water the edge runs in straight lines that line up with the edge beside them, with no notches. Only water is added to join the pieces: no county and no stop.

The government's definitions are in the US Census Bureau's [delineation files](https://www.census.gov/geographies/reference-files/time-series/demo/metro-micro/delineation-files.html).

## New York Metropolitan Area

- **Government's area:** the New York–Newark, NY-NJ-CT-PA combined statistical area (30 counties and Connecticut planning regions).
- **Added:** South Central Connecticut (New Haven), Naugatuck Valley (Waterbury), Lower Connecticut River Valley and Southeastern Connecticut (New London), which the government puts in the New Haven–Hartford–Waterbury combined area. Metro-North's New Haven Line and Waterbury Branch run there from New York, and Shore Line East continues the New Haven Line east to New London (rule 5).
- [Counties and operators](data-sources/new-york.md)

## Philadelphia Metropolitan Area

- **Government's area:** the Philadelphia–Reading–Camden, PA-NJ-DE-MD combined statistical area (16 counties).
- **Changes:** none.
- [Counties and operators](data-sources/philadelphia.md)

## Lehigh Valley

- **Government's area:** the Allentown–Bethlehem–East Stroudsburg, PA-NJ combined statistical area (5 counties).
- **Changes:** none.
- [Counties and operators](data-sources/lehigh-valley.md)

## Greater Boston

- **Government's area:** the Boston–Worcester–Providence, MA-RI-NH combined statistical area (18 counties).
- **Added:** York County, ME, which the government puts in the Portland–Lewiston–South Portland, ME combined area. COAST's buses from Dover and Portsmouth run to Berwick, South Berwick, Eliot and the Portsmouth Naval Shipyard in Kittery (rule 7).
- **Added:** Dukes County (Martha's Vineyard, Chappaquiddick and the Elizabeth Islands, with Cuttyhunk) and Nantucket County, MA, which the government leaves out of every combined area. The ferries to them leave from Woods Hole, Falmouth, Hyannis, Harwich Port and New Bedford, and in summer from Quonset Point, RI (rule 4).
- [Counties and operators](data-sources/greater-boston.md)

## Greater Hartford

- **Government's area:** the New Haven–Hartford–Waterbury, CT combined statistical area (7 planning regions).
- **Left out:** South Central Connecticut (New Haven), Naugatuck Valley (Waterbury), Lower Connecticut River Valley and Southeastern Connecticut (New London), which are part of the New York Metropolitan Area: the trains from New York run to them (rule 5). Greater Hartford is the other three planning regions: Capitol, Northeastern Connecticut and Northwest Hills.
- [Counties and operators](data-sources/greater-hartford.md)

## Western Massachusetts

- **Government's area:** the Springfield–Amherst Town–Northampton, MA combined statistical area (3 counties).
- **Added:** Berkshire County, which the government makes a metro area of its own (Pittsfield, MA), in no combined area. It is joined with the Pioneer Valley as Western Massachusetts (rules 3 and 5): the Link413 buses run from Pittsfield and North Adams to Greenfield and Northampton, and Amtrak's trains from Springfield stop in Pittsfield.
- [Counties and operators](data-sources/western-massachusetts.md)
